It is next submitted that proceeding was initiated for recovery of the rice and recovery citation was also issued, which was challenged before the writ Court, in which, the due amount of Rs.
79,47,947.58/- was ordered to be paid within a period of six months, but due to pandemic COVID-19, the said amount could not be deposited.
Thereafter, F.I.R. of the case in question was lodged and interim protection was granted by the writ Court, and then charge-sheet was submitted by Investigating Officer.

It is also submitted that the applicant is continuously refunding the aforesaid amount in installments, therefore, indulgence of this Court is required.
4.

Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposes the prayer of the applicant and submits that the protection was granted by the writ Court with direction that the amount be deposited within a period of six months, but the same could not be complied with, and no relaxation was requested before the writ Court.

He also submits that as it is a clear case of Section 409 I.P.C., there is no illegality in the charge-sheet as well as in the cognizance order, in such circumstances, the present application is liable to be dismissed.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and going through the contents of the application, F.I.R. as well as other relevant documents including order passed by the writ Court,
it is evident that time was granted to the applicant for depositing the due amount within a period of six months, but the same is not deposited.
6. Therefore, the present application is misconceived, accordingly, the same stands dismissed.
